Let's scrutinize spec against our code more.

- "Initial Launch (COUNTDOWN State — Exactly 3.000s Wall-Clock): Start COUNTDOWN on the first requestAnimationFrame callback after the initial resting scene (simTime=0.000) has rendered (countdownElapsed=0), advancing countdownElapsed by clamped wall dt... each frame so cold-start shader compilation never skips '3'."
  - Our initial resting render is synchronous before the first rAF. First rAF callback starts countdown (sets lastTimestamp, show3) but does NOT advance countdownElapsed. From then each frame advances. The 3 seconds begin on the second rAF. So effectively countdown lasts3 seconds plus one frame after the first rAF. "Start COUNTDOWN on first rAF ... advancing ... each frame" might imply first frame should advance by dt; but rawDt since no prior. Practically exactly wall3 plus one frame. Fine.
  - On first render, `#countdown` is already visible3 from markup. good.

- "simTime remains0.000 and scrubber.value remains '0'." Our code does not alter simTime; it calls renderAt0 and leaves scrubber value "0". At countdown display frames, the rAF branch doesn't update scrubber. Good. However our `enterPlaying` at transition sets scrubber.value = "0.000"; this occurs when countdown elapsed >=3, so no longer in countdown. good.

var overflow = countdownElapsed - 3;
countdownElapsed=3;
hideCountdown();
enterPlaying(0); // sets state and renders0
